$comment: IDL for the Path of Dust replay bundle. THIS FILE IS THE SOURCE OF TRUTH. The Rust conformance checks (game/src/adventure/replay_bundle/schema.rs) and the JavaScript validator (replay-bundle-validator.js, delivered to PathOfDust_Desktop by PR) are both derived from it; a test fails the build if either drifts. Hand-edit this, then run tools/gen-bundle-validator.mjs.

readerRules.$comment: Forward compatibility is mandatory, not optional: four surfaces version independently (Rust server, overlay.html which deploys with it, the desktop's hot-pulled index.html, and server.mjs which runs until restart), so an old reader and a new writer are always live at the same time.

memberStates.$comment: A reader that only sees a missing key cannot tell 'this aged out' from 'this was never produced'. Those are different answers to an audit question, so the manifest names the state explicitly.

tiers.$comment: Exposure tiers. /overlay and /ws are public and unauthenticated by design; anything above public must never be reachable from them.

realDurationMs.$comment: BOTH durations ride the manifest. events[].atMs is display-compressed while rolls[].atMs is real; recovering real tick times means inverting that transform, which is impossible without the ratio.

pinned.$comment: Pinned bundles are exempt from per-member expiry and carry their own 256 MB cap, separate from the 2 GB detail budget.

v.$comment: Per-member version, so one member can evolve alone.

pinnedShape.$comment: true only on playerVitals: its shape never advances without an explicit external-consumer migration.

core.$comment: Everything about the fight that is not an event stream. Measured at under 0.1% of an archive file, so nothing here is worth splitting further.

replay.$comment: One merged, ordered stream. These four kinds are exactly what overlay.html's fireEvent has branches for, and exactly what the server still broadcasts after the 2026-08-20 thinning rework.

buffs.$comment: Split out of replay deliberately. shield+buffSnapshot are 25.16% of archive event bytes and were removed from the public broadcast on purpose; they come back only behind a session, never onto /ws. The companion app has live code for both and is starved of them today.

dot.$comment: Aggregated in the archive per (attacker,target) window - measured 98.34% fewer records. Full fidelity on the wire subset, which the per-second attack budget has already capped.

rolls.$comment: Never aggregated, never public. 66.8% of an archive file. Joins back to replay on eventId.

playerVitals.$comment: PINNED BYTE-FOR-BYTE at its current shape and path. The external consumer is PathOfDust_Desktop; this release does not touch it, and its version never advances without an explicit migration agreed with that consumer. It is 0.01% of an archive file - there is no saving here worth breaking someone else's app for.

hpSamples.$comment: [atMs, hp] pairs, bucketed to 100ms, last-write-wins inside a bucket.

eventKinds.$comment: Every record additionally carries the member's sequenceKey (seq): a fight-scoped, dense, monotonic index stamped from the events array at write time. atMs is NOT unique and hitId is absent on five of these six kinds and non-monotonic besides, so neither can order a replay - measured 2026-08-20.
